title: 用 A 写 KCL 和 KVL
statement: 电路如图（V_s1 = 10 V，I_s5 = 1 A，R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω，R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω，R_6 = 8 Ω）。画有向图时把 V_s1 与 R_1 的串联看成一条支路（支路 1），把 R_5 与 I_s5 的并联看成一条支路（支路 5），其余每个电阻一条支路；结点编号 1、2、3、4（4 接地），支路编号与方向见下方的有向图。
参考结点为 4，A 的行、列顺序与上一题相同。已知结点电压 V_n1 = 6.8 V、V_n2 = 2.4 V、V_n3 = 2.8 V（对结点 4）。支路电压 V_k、电流 I_k 都按有向图的支路方向（V_k 从支路起点量到终点，与 I_k 关联）。用 V = Aᵀ·V_n 求支路电压，用 A·I = 0 求一个支路电流。

questions.ask: 支路电压 V_1 = ?（按支路 1 的方向，由 4 指向 1）
questions.explain: V = Aᵀ·V_n 的第 1 行：A 的第 1 列只有 a_11 = −1，所以 V_1 = −V_n1 = −6.8 V（支路电压从起点量到终点：V_1 = v_4 − v_1）。

questions.ask: 已知 I_1 = 1.6 A、I_2 = 1.1 A，用 A·I = 0 的第 1 行求 I_6。
A·I = 0 和 V = Aᵀ·V_n 分别是什么？
choices: 前者是 KVL，后者是欧姆定律
两者都只对电阻电路成立
前者是 n − 1 个独立结点的 KCL，后者是 KVL（支路电压用结点电压表示）
choiceExplain: A·I = 0 是电流的约束（KCL），V = Aᵀ·V_n 与元件无关，不是欧姆定律。
两式只由拓扑决定，与元件性质无关，对任何集中参数电路都成立。
对：A 的第 j 行乘 I 就是结点 j 流出电流之和；V = Aᵀ·V_n 说每条支路电压等于起点与终点结点电压之差——这自动满足 KVL。
questions.explain: 拓扑约束只用 A：KCL A·I = 0，KVL V = Aᵀ·V_n。

hints: V = Aᵀ·V_n：第 k 个支路电压 = A 的第 k 列与 V_n 的点积。
A·I = 0 的第 1 行就是结点 1 的 KCL（流出为正）。

en.title: KCL and KVL with A
statement: The circuit is drawn below (V_s1 = 10 V, I_s5 = 1 A, R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω, R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω, R_6 = 8 Ω). In the graph, V_s1 in series with R_1 counts as one branch (branch 1), R_5 in parallel with I_s5 as one branch (branch 5), and each other resistor as one branch; the nodes are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 (4 is grounded) and the branch numbers and directions are those of the directed graph under the circuit.

The reference is node 4, rows and columns of A as in the previous problem. The node voltages are V_n1 = 6.8 V, V_n2 = 2.4 V, V_n3 = 2.8 V (to node 4). Branch voltages V_k and currents I_k follow the branch directions of the graph (V_k measured from the start to the end of branch k, associated with I_k). Use V = Aᵀ·V_n for branch voltages and A·I = 0 for a branch current.

questions.ask: Branch voltage V_1 = ? (along branch 1, from 4 to 1)
questions.explain: Row 1 of V = Aᵀ·V_n: column 1 of A has only a_11 = −1, so V_1 = −V_n1 = −6.8 V (a branch voltage is measured from its start to its end: V_1 = v_4 − v_1).

questions.ask: Given I_1 = 1.6 A and I_2 = 1.1 A, use row 1 of A·I = 0 to find I_6.
What are A·I = 0 and V = Aᵀ·V_n?
choices: the first is KVL, the second is Ohm's law
both hold only for resistive circuits
the first is KCL at the n − 1 independent nodes, the second is KVL (branch voltages in terms of node voltages)
choiceExplain: A·I = 0 constrains currents (KCL); V = Aᵀ·V_n involves no element law.
Both come from topology alone and hold for any lumped circuit.
Right: row j of A times I is the sum of currents leaving node j; V = Aᵀ·V_n says each branch voltage is the difference of its end node voltages — which satisfies KVL automatically.
questions.explain: The topological laws need only A: KCL A·I = 0, KVL V = Aᵀ·V_n.

hints: V = Aᵀ·V_n: branch voltage k is column k of A dotted with V_n.
Row 1 of A·I = 0 is KCL at node 1 (leaving = positive).
solution: **Check:** branch 6 is R_6 = 8 Ω alone, I_6 = V_6/R_6 = 4/8 = 0.5 A ✓ (both routes agree).
